evidence: This is a quantitative result from the comparison of datasets.

claim: The correlation between LRz and AB values is striking when considering the fact that the values are derived from experiments that differ greatly in their approaches, species, and cell types.
source: These correlations are even more striking when considering the fact that the LRz and AB values are derived from experiments that differ greatly in their approaches (mechanical subcellular fractionation vs. proximity labeling), species (mouse vs. human), and cell types (neurons vs. intestinal epithelial cells).
evidence: This is an observation about the robustness of the correlation.

claim: The basal compartment of epithelial cells and the neurites of neurons are spatial equivalents, at least in terms of RNA localization.
source: These very different cellular compartments are therefore spatial equivalents, at least in terms of RNA localization
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the similarity of RNA contents.

claim: The RNA contents of the basal compartment of epithelial cells and the neurites of neurons are likely governed by the same regulatory mechanisms.
source: These very different cellular compartments are therefore spatial equivalents, at least in terms of RNA localization, and their RNA contents are likely governed by the same regulatory mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference from the similarity of RNA contents.

claim: The most enriched GO terms for genes localized basally in enterocytes and to the neurites of neurons were 'ribosome' and 'mitochondrion'.
source: The genes that fall in the fourth quadrant of Figure 6F are localized basally in enterocytes and to the neurites of neurons. To interrogate the identity of these genes we used GO enrichment analysis (Alexa, 2010). The most enriched GO terms were 'ribosome' and 'mitochondrion' (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result from GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Mitochondria are enriched toward the basal pole of epithelial cells.
source: We have similarly found that mitochondria are enriched toward the basal pole of epithelial cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 8)
evidence: This is based on imaging experiments.

claim: Mitochondria have been previously reported to be found in neuronal projections.
source: We have similarly found that mitochondria are enriched toward the basal pole of epithelial cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 8), and mitochondria have previously been reported to be found in neuronal projections (Mandal and Drerup, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Many nuclear-encoded RNAs that encode mitochondrial proteins are translated on the surface of the mitochondria.
source: Given that many nuclear-encoded RNAs that encode mitochondrial proteins are translated on the surface of the mitochondria
evidence: This is a statement about known biology.

claim: It may be expected that nuclear-encoded RNAs that encode mitochondrial proteins are neurite- and basal-enriched.
source: Given that many nuclear-encoded RNAs that encode mitochondrial proteins are translated on the surface of the mitochondria, it may be expected that these RNAs are also neurite- and basal-enriched.
evidence: This is an inference based on mitochondrial localization.

claim: RNAs that encode components of the electron transport chain (ETC) were both neurite- and basal-enriched according to the sequencing data sets.
source: Consistent with this idea, we found that RNAs that encode components of the electron transport chain (ETC) were both neurite- and basal-enriched according to our sequencing data sets (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the sequencing datasets.

claim: Similarities in RNA localization between epithelial and neuronal cells can be driven by similar organelle localization.
source: This suggests that similarities in RNA localization between these two cell types can be driven by similar organelle localization.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of mitochondrial RNA localization.

claim: Intestinal epithelial cells and neurons are organized using similar underlying microtubule structures.
source: Despite drastically different morphologies, intestinal epithelial cells and neurons are organized using similar underlying microtubule structures.
evidence: This is a statement about cell biology.

claim: Microtubules are organized such that their plus ends are oriented basally in intestinal epithelial cells and out to neurite tips in neurons.
source: These polar molecules are organized in such a way that their plus ends are oriented basally in intestinal epithelial cells and out to neurite tips in neurons (Müsch, 2004; Sugioka and Sawa, 2012; Yogev et al., 2016; Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: RNAs are known to be trafficked along microtubules.
source: Because of the similar microtubule architecture in both cell types and the fact that RNAs are known to be trafficked along microtubules (Cross et al., 2021; Gagnon and Mowry, 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: RNAs were hypothesized to be trafficked to neurites and the basal pole of epithelial cells through the action of kinesin motor proteins.
source: Because of the similar microtubule architecture in both cell types and the fact that RNAs are known to be trafficked along microtubules (Cross et al., 2021; Gagnon and Mowry, 2011), we hypothesized that RNAs were being trafficked to neurites and the basal pole of epithelial cells through the action of kinesin motor proteins.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on known biology.

claim: Kinesin inhibition dramatically reduced the basal localization of reporter RNAs containing the Net1 3′ UTR in C2bbe1 monolayers.
source: Cells expressing the full length Net1 3′ UTR reporter construct were treated for four hours with kinesore or ciliobrevin A, a dynein-1 inhibitor. In C2bbe1 monolayers, we found that kinesin inhibition dramatically reduced the basal localization of reporter RNAs containing the Net1 3′ UTR (Figure 7B and C)
evidence: This is based on smFISH experiments following drug treatment.

claim: The effect of kinesin inhibition on Net1 3′ UTR reporter localization was specific to the Net1 3′ UTR.
source: This effect was specific to the Net1 3′ UTR as the localization of reporter transcripts lacking the 3′ UTR was unaffected by kinesin inhibition (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on smFISH experiments following drug treatment.

claim: Inhibition of dynein strengthens basal localization of Net1 3′ UTR transcripts.
source: Interestingly, we found that inhibition of dynein strengthens basal localization of Net1 3′ UTR transcripts.
evidence: This is based on smFISH experiments following drug treatment.

claim: Kinesin and dynein activity are often closely linked, pulling the same cargoes in different directions.
source: Kinesin and dynein activity are often closely linked, pulling the same cargoes in different directions.
evidence: This is a statement about motor protein biology.

claim: When the activity of one motor protein is inhibited, it can increase the apparent activity of the other.
source: When the activity of one motor is inhibited, it can therefore increase the apparent activity of the other (Soppina et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In neuronal cells, kinesin inhibition significantly reduced the neurite localization of the Net1 3′ UTR reporter RNAs.
source: In neuronal cells, kinesin inhibition again significantly reduced the neurite localization of the Net1 3′ UTR reporter RNAs, again suggesting they are transported along microtubules (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is based on smFISH experiments following drug treatment.

claim: No changes in the localization of the control Firefly luciferase reporter transcript were observed in response to drug treatments.
source: We did not observe any changes in the localization of our control reporter transcript, Firefly luciferase, in response to drug treatments (Figure 7—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is based on smFISH experiments following drug treatment.

claim: Changes in Net1 reporter RNA localization in neuronal cells were driven by changes in RNA content of the neurite and not any gross changes in expression.
source: Additionally, as before, changes in RNA localization were driven by changes in RNA content of the neurite and not any gross changes in expression (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on analysis of transcript abundance.

claim: In C2bbe1 monolayers, kinesin inhibition removed the basal localization of both RPL7 and RPS28 PRRE reporter constructs.
source: We found very similar results with our PRRE reporter transcripts when inhibiting motor proteins. In C2bbe1 monolayers, kinesin inhibition removed the basal localization of both RPL7 and RPS28 PRRE reporter constructs (Figure 7F, Figure 7—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on smFISH experiments following drug treatment.

claim: Kinesin-mediated transport along microtubules was required for the neurite localization of PRRE-containing transcripts.
source: Kinesin-mediated transport along microtubules was also required for the neurite localization of PRRE-containing transcripts (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is based on smFISH experiments following drug treatment.

claim: Changes in PRRE reporter RNA abundance in neuronal cells were neurite-specific and were not observed cell-wide.
source: Once again, changes in RNA abundance were neurite-specific and were not observed cell-wide (Figure 7—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on analysis of transcript abundance.

claim: The RNA contents of neurites and the basal pole of epithelial cells are determined at least in part through microtubule plus-end directed trafficking mechanisms.
source: Given that the plus ends of microtubules are associated with both neurites and the basal pole of epithelial cells and that kinesin inhibition reduced RNA localization to both compartments, we conclude that the RNA contents of both locations are determined at least in part through microtubule plus-end directed trafficking mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the kinesin inhibition experiments.
